_why: Every price the catalog shows comes from this file. One place, so an
estimate can never be half-updated, and so the assumption is reviewable
rather than buried in a template.
THESE ARE NOT QUOTES. They are a published industry band for FDM service
pricing, and nothing here has been checked against a real order. The whole
point of showing an estimate is to tell someone whether a build is a $50
decision or a $400 one before they get invested, and a number that is wrong
by 3x does that worse than no number at all.
To replace them with something real: npm run quote-bundle <slug> makes a zip
a provider's quote page will accept. Put one through, then set `source` and
`quoted` below to what came back and narrow the band to match.
source: industry band for FDM service pricing, $0.10-0.50/cm3

PETG.note: The common case. Every FDM service carries it.

CF-nylon.note: Carbon-filled nylon is an industrial-FDM material, not a desktop one. Protolabs Network quotes it as Markforged Onyx, which is a specific product rather than a generic PA-CF: confirm the substitution before quoting it as equivalent.

TPU 95A.note: Services quote TPU by shore hardness and the common service grade is 88A, softer than the 95A these packs specify. Treat a TPU quote as a substitution until confirmed.

setup_note: Per order, not per part. Services charge a floor that dominates a small order: it is most of the cost of printing one bracket and almost none of the cost of a whole body.
_pricing_model: estimate = setup_usd + sum over parts of (volume_cm3 x qty x usd_per_cm3)
Volume is the solid figure from the STL, which is what a service prices on:
they choose their own walls and infill, so the printed mass that matters to
someone running their own printer is not the number a service bills.
